name: Brickellia

project_scope.learner_admission: Approved Master Plant Pool; both UNRESOLVED; B. eupatorioides var. gracillima represented by species concept.

look_here_first: Inspect leaf nodes, then the lower leaf surface, layered phyllaries of a mature head, and finally mature cypsela and pappus under magnification.

comparison.eupatorioides: Usually opposite, but alternate in some varieties.
Variable across varieties; not diagnosed by dense lower-face tomentum alone.

comparison.cylindracea: Check mature bristles and cypsela hairs against FNA.
Often opposite/subopposite leaves and pale-tomentose lower surface.
comparison.dentata: Alternate leaves; 18–22 phyllaries in 5–6 series; 13–20 disk florets; mature cypsela mostly glabrous, 3.5–4 mm.
comparison.eupatorioides: Phyllotaxy variable across varieties; mature pappus plumose/subplumose.

cautions: B. eupatorioides var. gracillima is nested; do not create an unreviewed duplicate card.
Both installed species remain UNRESOLVED for target-zone range; no confirmed-native credit.
B. dentata is already canonical; B. eupatorioides var. gracillima remains represented under the species concept. All three have unresolved range labels.
visual_status: Provisional comparison; macro photos of nodes, heads, and mature fruits needed.
shared_genus_traits: Heads consist of disc florets, with overlapping involucral phyllaries and cypselae bearing pappus bristles.
Examine mature heads, pappus and leaf surfaces together; no single leaf character separates every species.
Three canonical species; heads discoid with layered phyllaries and pappus-bearing cypselae.

genus_diagnostics.look_here_first: Inspect leaf nodes, then the lower leaf surface, layered phyllaries of a mature head, and finally mature cypsela and pappus under magnification.

shared_structures.plain: A flower head made of tiny tubular florets, not a single flower.
shared_structures.photo_role: mature head face and side macro
shared_structures.why: Count disk florets and recognize the genus.

shared_structures.photo_role: side profile with ruler showing outer and inner bracts
shared_structures.why: Series count and relative bract lengths distinguish species.

shared_structures.plain: Feltlike hairs and tiny glands under the leaf.
shared_structures.photo_role: matched leaf undersides and intact nodes
shared_structures.why: Hairiness and leaf attachment help separate B. cylindracea and B. dentata.

shared_structures.plain: A dry seedlike fruit with bristles.
shared_structures.why: Fruit hairs and pappus texture help settle look-alikes.

comparison_cards.title: Cylindracea versus dentata
comparison_cards.look_first: Check several intact leaf nodes and undersides.
comparison_cards.difference: B. cylindracea often has opposite/subopposite leaves with dense pale hairs beneath; B. dentata has alternate leaves and mostly glabrous ripe cypselae.
comparison_cards.caution: Involucre sizes and phyllary numbers overlap; fruit macro is valuable.

comparison_cards.title: Dentata versus eupatorioides
comparison_cards.look_first: Examine mature head and fruit, not just leaf arrangement.
comparison_cards.difference: B. dentata commonly has 13–20 disk florets and mostly glabrous 3.5–4 mm cypselae; B. eupatorioides has variable head counts and plumose/subplumose pappus.
comparison_cards.caution: Some B. eupatorioides varieties have alternate leaves. Do not infer variety from one source-pool name.
